subject: Kiosk data: privacy-preserving hashing for EU events
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmeconf.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: integrations@scantech.io
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kiosk data: privacy-preserving hashing for EU events

Hi Logan,

Hope you're well — we're finalizing privacy controls for our September EU roadshow and want to confirm how Redwood can support privacy-preserving lead capture from onsite badge scanners/kiosk tablets. Our legal team is requiring: 1) PII never leave the device in plaintext, 2) a 30-day retention TTL for scanned leads, and 3) a deterministic hashed key we can use to deduplicate across our CRM (HubSpot) without sharing raw emails.

Two quick questions for your team:
- Can badge scanners perform a one-way hash (or tokenization) on-device before sending to Redwood?
- If so, can Redwood accept a salted hash and map it server-side to a HubSpot contact without storing the raw email?

Attached is our hardware spec and a short note from our privacy team. We're willing to have ScanTech (our scanner vendor, cc'd) implement client-side behavior but need Redwood's integration requirements.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Field Operations, Acme Conferences
(attachment: acme-event-hardware-specs.pdf)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmeconf.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kiosk data: privacy-preserving hashing for EU events

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the spec. Short answer: yes, we can support a privacy-preserving flow that meets your constraints. Below is a proposed approach and a few open decisions.

Summary of proposed flow:
- On-device hashing: scanners perform SHA-256 on the email/PII, then apply an event-specific salt (unique per-event/per-day) before sending. That matches your "PII never leaves device in plaintext" requirement.
- Ephemeral salt rotation: devices rotate salts daily (or per-session) and include a salt-id in the payload; salts are not reversible and are rotated so long-term re-identification is minimized.
- HMAC + server-side sealing: Redwood receives the salted hash and computes an HMAC using a Redwood-held key (KMS-backed). The HMAC is the canonical key we store for dedupe and mapping to HubSpot. Raw PII is never stored.
- TTL & deletion: tokens/hashes are stored for a 30-day TTL, then purged. We can provide an audit log for deletion events to satisfy compliance evidence requests.
- HubSpot sync: we can send the HMAC key to a HubSpot unique-identifier field. If Acme wants to perform matching, we can provide a service to compute the same HMAC on your side (shared secret) or accept that HubSpot will contain only the hashed identifier for dedupe.

Open questions / risks:
- If you need cross-event deduping (same person across multiple events), per-event salt will prevent matching. We can support a "global event salt" option but that weakens cross-event unlinkability.
- ScanTech needs to confirm they can implement SHA-256 + salt. If devices are constrained we can provide an SDK or cloud-edge gateway to accept plaintext from the scanner over a secure local network and perform hashing there — but that is less ideal for the "PII never leaves device" ask.
- Legal: confirm that HMAC with Redwood-held key is acceptable for you; otherwise we can design a flow where Acme holds a secret and computes the HMAC client-side so Redwood never has the key.

Next steps I propose:
1) ScanTech confirm capability (integration@scantech.io).
2) Redwood sends an "edge-hash-spec.pdf" (attached) with payload format, salt-id header, and sample HubSpot mapping.
3) Quick 30-min call tomorrow to confirm cross-event dedupe and secret management.

I've attached our draft spec and a sample HubSpot mapping sheet. Marissa — can you pick a 30-min slot tomorrow morning PT? Rafael / Neha — flag any security/legal blockers.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
(attachment: edge-hash-spec.pdf; attachment: hubspot-mapping-draft.xlsx)

Thanks Logan — looks good to me. Two quick notes:
- MarCom will want standardized consent language on the scanner UI (we can reuse the short opt-in line we use for EU events) — I’ll share the exact copy in the Drive link you listed.
- For HubSpot mapping, Rafael and I will update the ingestion playbook to map the HMAC->Contact.external_id and add a flag that the contact was created via hashed-kiosk. Ops should mark those contacts as candidates for automatic merge within 7 days if we see a matching hashed id.

Emily — can you confirm ScanTech's timeline? If they're good to implement SHA-256+salt rotation this week we can run a small pilot (single venue) the first week of August. Otherwise we can stand up the edge-gateway option as a fallback.

Marissa Cole
